pairs.translation:
If mindfulness becomes distracted,
whether virtuous, nonvirtuous, or ethically indeterminate,
whichever of these three differentiating conceptualizations arises,
do not reject it; regard it as a great kindness.
Regard it as necessary and indispensable,
and as a very great kindness. [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C002](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c002) [N-C003](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c003) [N-C036](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c036)

Once you know it in this way,
since the supreme means for realizing dharma embodiment
is differentiating conceptualization itself,
and differentiating conceptualization is the dregs of ordinary mind,
the དོང་པོ་ of conceptual thought becomes dharma embodiment.
“Thus, differentiating conceptualization is a great marvel!”
Know this vividly and clearly. [N-C004](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c004)

Conceptual thought is ordinary mind itself, non-arising;
rest undistracted in the state of emptiness. [N-C005](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c005)

Or, when differentiating conceptualization arises,
like sunlight and the scent of sandalwood,
ordinary mind, conceptual thought, and dharma embodiment—these three—
are not separate;
they abide like water and its waves.
Having known this vividly and clearly,
rest in equipoise in the uncontrived state. [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C006](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c006)

Once you have rested in the uncontrived state,
all differentiating conceptualizations, without exception,
will certainly dissipate like clouds in space.

From the precious venerable one—ཞལ་ལྔ་ནས་ [attribution unresolved]:
“We all take differentiating conceptualization onto the path.
Others wish to reject conceptual thought.
Those who wish to reject conceptual thought
must reject the nature of phenomena, great bliss;
if ordinary mind itself is rejected, dharma embodiment
will be rejected—there is no doubt.
Therefore, remain undistracted and take it onto the path.” [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C005](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c005) [N-C007](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c007) [N-C008](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c008) [N-C031](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c031)

In “The Complete Purity of the Perfections”:
“The differentiating conceptualization of afflicted samsara
and omniscient primordial knowing—these two—
are nondual, one in intrinsic nature,
with not the slightest difference,” it is said. [N-C009](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c009) [N-C029](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c029)

In the tantras of Mahamudra:
“However one has been burned by fire,
one should approach that very fire.
However differentiating conceptualization arises,
one should rely on that very conceptual thought.
Through craving, craving is purified;
through conceptual thought itself, conceptual thought is cleared away.
That very conceptual thought is taught as the means.” [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C008](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c008) [N-C010](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c010) [N-C011](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c011) [N-C038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c038)

In a vajra song, it is said:
“This coemergent consciousness—
how is it to be apprehended as primordial knowing?
When certain knowing arises, that very thing is seen.
This differentiating conceptualization that arises in oneself—
how is it to be apprehended as dharma embodiment?
When one has experiential acquaintance with it, its core is seen.” [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C012](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c012)

The great teacher said:
“Since afflictions are primordial knowing itself,
there is no need to cultivate an antidote separately.
Understanding self-arising is the supreme means.
Like the fruit of smṛta [unidentified],
from the very time of the cause it abides as the result.” [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C013](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c013) [N-C028](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c028) [N-C029](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c029) [N-C038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c038)

When various differentiating conceptualizations arise,
know them to be like the peacock’s food.
Cultivating the three kinds of discerning knowing at that time has been taught. [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001)

Fifth, how experiences arise:
having taken conceptual thought onto the path,
if you cultivate in four successive sessions,
meeting someone known before, [snow] on a hot stone,
a forest burned by fire, and bliss and clarity-emptiness—
in brief, four kinds of experiential acquaintance are said to arise. [N-C014](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c014) [N-C031](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c031)

First, meeting someone known before:
for example, when two dear friends
suddenly meet upon a road,
just as they recognize each other at the very moment of meeting,
so that yogin too,
at the very moment differentiating conceptualization arises,
comes to certainty that their own ordinary mind is empty.
This is called “overcoming upon encounter,” it is said. [N-C014](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c014) [N-C016](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c016)

Second, snow on a hot stone:
although snow comes from clouds,
as soon as it falls upon a hot stone,
at that very moment it turns to water.
Likewise, if conceptual thought arises from distraction,
immediately after arising it is known as ordinary mind.
Of ordinary mind itself as dharma embodiment, free from conceptual elaborations,
[realization] arises without effort.
This is called “overcoming upon encounter.” [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C005](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c005) [N-C015](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c015) [N-C016](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c016)

Third, a forest burned by fire:
for example, when a forest catches fire,
trees, grass, sentient beings,
clean and unclean places, and so forth—
it burns them without realization [wording uncertain].
Whatever wind or hail arises,
far from dying out, the fire is further helped. [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C017](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c017) [N-C030](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c030)

Likewise, as soon as the great fire of realization blazes,
various good and bad differentiating conceptualizations,
apprehended object and apprehending subject, afflictions, attachment, aversion, and so forth—
without accepting and rejecting, denying and affirming—
it burns them in the state of non-arising.
The more differentiating conceptualizations there are,
the more they aid the arising of realization.
This is called “fire emanation.” [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C018](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c018) [N-C029](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c029) [N-C036](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c036)

Once realization is stable in this way,
it is clear, unceasing, and free from extremes,
without clinging to bliss, clarity, or non-conceptuality.
Even if pierced by a needle, bliss arises.
Day and night, in sessions and between them, walking, sitting, and so forth—
if there is no difference in any mode of activity,
this is the fourth experiential acquaintance, bliss and clarity.
These are the ways experiences arise. [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C031](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c031)

Of these, first, the benefits:
upon cultivation, the view arises;
upon the view, cultivation arises;
view and cultivation arise as one taste.
This is described as “diverse appearances.”
Marks are liberated in their own place,
and since the time of the cause and the result are the same,
there is “entry of intrinsic nature into dharma” [reading uncertain]. [N-C020](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c020) [N-C032](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c032) [N-C038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c038)

You will live on the food of deep absorption;
obstacles and māras will be unable to assail you.
Supernormal knowing will arise,
and you will see buddha fields, and so forth.
All such common benefits
will arise of their own force, without obstruction. [N-C021](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c021) [N-C037](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c037)

Even when all these qualities, without exception,
have arisen completely within you,
know them to be temporary results;
do not regard them as supreme marvels,
but exert yourself and cultivate without interruption. [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001)

Do not follow conceptual thought.
Know differentiating conceptualization as ordinary mind;
ordinary mind itself is non-arising, free from conceptual elaborations.
Cultivate non-conceptuality, bliss, and clarity lucidly.
Remaining undistracted in that state is supreme cultivation. [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C005](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c005) [N-C031](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c031) [N-C037](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c037)

Even if conceptual thought arises,
do not regard it as faulty:
when its intrinsic nature is known, it is dharma embodiment. [N-C008](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c008)

Those who desire a cultivation superior to this
and wish to seek it elsewhere
fall into the two, hope and fear.
Hope obstructs all qualities;
if fear is present, it binds one to samsara.
There is no realization and no bliss or clarity.
Even if there is good abiding,
the venerable one calls it “a path of deviation.” [N-C022](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c022) [N-C031](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c031) [N-C029](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c029)

Second, enhancement through activity:
the supreme result will arise.
In going, walking, lying down, and every mode of activity,
activity inseparable from cultivation is supreme. [N-C035](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c035)

From engaging in such activity come
one-pointedness, freedom from conceptual elaborations, one taste,
and perfected non-cultivation; among the results,
realization of the result as one taste,
without hope and fear, is the supreme result. [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C025](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c025) [N-C032](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c032)

Yet, in the appearances of those to be trained,
blazing with the major and minor marks,
naturally arising Shakyamuni and the others
are form embodiments that act for sentient beings’ benefit. [N-C026](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c026) [N-C030](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c030) [N-C033](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c033) [N-C037](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c037) [N-C038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c038)

Like a vase, a great wish-fulfilling tree,
and a wish-fulfilling jewel,
without conceptual thought, according to beings’
wishes, they teach dharma:
this is stated often in the great tantras.
That is what is called the result. [N-C010](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c010) [N-C037](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c037) [N-C038](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c038)
These are the benefits and results.

With the general meaning arranged in six aspects,
in accordance with the lord’s spoken words,
with four conditions and the donning of two armors,
these pith instructions on coemergent joining
were composed for the benefit of both myself and others.
Dakinis and dharma protectors, please forgive! [N-C001](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c001) [N-C032](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c032) [N-C034](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c034) [N-C037](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c037)

Through the virtue of writing this,
may all the limitless sentient beings, without exception,
realize differentiating conceptualization as dharma embodiment! [N-C030](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c030)
This completes Coemergent Joining, composed by the wanderer Dor Gyal. Śubhaṃ—may it be auspicious. [N-C027](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c027) [N-C032](../translations/NOTES.md#n-c032)

notes.problem: Twenty lines contain duplicated vowel signs in the frozen electronic transcript. These are not the legacy tokenization markers.
notes.treatment: English provisionally interprets the repeated vowel signs as single signs in the corresponding syllables; all source strings remain unchanged.
notes.uncertainty: The likely intended syllables are generally clear, but no physical witness has been checked. This note does not authenticate corrections.
notes.review_action: Compare these exact anchors against a physical witness or independently established transcript before any Tibetan correction.

notes.problem: The glossary assigns ལུང་མ་བསྟན་ to stagnant neutrality. Here it is the third member of a virtue/nonvirtue classification; stagnant neutrality would impose a particular meditative fault on an ethical category.
notes.treatment: Use ethically indeterminate provisionally only for this member of the threefold classification; retain differentiating conceptualization for རྣམ་རྟོག་.
notes.uncertainty: The construction strongly supports ethical indeterminacy; this exception has not been approved.
notes.review_action: Approve or revise this occurrence-specific exception; leave the canonical glossary assignment unchanged.

notes.problem: དགེོས་ has mixed vowel signs and the line appears to express necessity and indispensability.
notes.treatment: Translate provisionally as necessary and indispensable, treating དགེོས་ as intended དགོས་ without altering the source.
notes.uncertainty: The intended necessity construction is probable; exact spelling and punctuation are unverified.
notes.review_action: Check the source for དགོས་དང་མེད་དུ་མི་རུང་ or another reading.

དེ་ལྟ་བུར་ནི་ཤེས་ཙམ་ན། །
ཆོས་སྐུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཐབས་ཀྱི་མཆོག །
རྣམ་རྟོག་ཁོ་རང་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར། །
སེམས་ཀྱི་སྙིགས་མ་རྣམ་རྟོག་སྟེ། །
རྟོག་པ་དོང་པོ་ཆོས་སྐུར་གྱུར། །
དེ་བས་རྣམ་རྟོག་ངོ་མཚར་ཆེ། །
སྙམ་དུ་ཝལ་གྱིས་ཤེས་པར་བྱ། །
notes.problem: The relation of རྟོག་པ་དོང་པོ་ to the preceding dregs statement is uncertain. དོང་པོ་ is not securely identified here. The old English first thought does not establish the Tibetan reading.
notes.treatment: Retain དོང་པོ་ visibly. The draft provisionally takes lines 399–403 as condition, causal explanation, and resulting clause; it preserves the final instruction to know the marvel vividly and clearly.
notes.uncertainty: The untranslated expression and the exact causal attachment remain unresolved; no replacement such as essence, original state, or first thought is asserted.
notes.review_action: Obtain witness evidence for L0403 and review the syntax of the full seven-line unit.

notes.problem: There is no whole-expression entry for སེམས་ཉིད་. The established སེམས་ is ordinary mind. སྐྱེ་མེད་ is also a contracted form of the established non-arising expression.
notes.treatment: Use ordinary mind itself for སེམས་ཉིད་ and non-arising for སྐྱེ་མེད་. Retain the full ordinary mind term in all relationships to dharma embodiment.
notes.uncertainty: The ordinary mind commitment is established; the lexical force of ཉིད་ and the contracted-form documentation remain proposed.
notes.review_action: Review a linked compound/construction record without silently substituting mind itself or nature of mind.

notes.problem: The compact analogies list sunlight and sandalwood scent before the threefold identification and water/waves analogy; the source does not separately spell out sun/rays or sandalwood/scent as four nouns.
notes.treatment: Preserve the compact analogy rather than silently adding an expanded explanation of its causal relations.
notes.uncertainty: Their relation is intelligible by analogy, but the precise pairing of the three items is not stated.
notes.review_action: Check the quotation or source if an expanded explanation is desired.

notes.problem: ཞལ་ལྔ་ནས་ literally suggests from five mouths/faces and is irregular as a speech-attribution formula. It does not securely identify five teachers.
notes.treatment: Translate the precious venerable one and retain ཞལ་ལྔ་ནས་ with an explicit unresolved marker.
notes.uncertainty: The quotation speaker and intended attribution formula remain uncertain.
notes.review_action: Check the reading and identify the quotation; do not identify five masters or replace the phrase silently.

notes.problem: Missing tshegs occur in ལམདུ་, གྱུརཀྱང་, བརགྱུར་, and ཆོསསྐུ་.
notes.treatment: English provisionally segments these as ལམ་དུ་, གྱུར་ཀྱང་, བར་གྱུར་, and ཆོས་སྐུ་; original source remains intact.
notes.uncertainty: High confidence in segmentation from local grammar, without witness verification.
notes.review_action: Verify the missing separators against a better source before editing Tibetan.

notes.problem: The phrase ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པའི་རྣམ་དག་ introduces a citation but does not establish a verified text title or include the words discerning knowing.
notes.treatment: Use the provisional quoted label The Complete Purity of the Perfections. Do not identify a particular perfection-of-discerning-knowing scripture.
notes.uncertainty: It may designate a passage or subject rather than a work title.
notes.review_action: Identify the citation and decide whether the label should be a title or descriptive phrase.

notes.problem: L0431 has ཕྱག་རྒུ་ rather than expected ཕྱག་རྒྱ་. The glossary assigns རྒྱུད་ to continuum, but both occurrences here refer to quoted literary sources.
notes.treatment: Interpret Mahamudra provisionally at L0431 and use tantras for this citation sense of རྒྱུད་.
notes.uncertainty: Mahamudra is highly probable; exact cited tantras and the scoped lexical exception are unverified.
notes.review_action: Check the title reading and approve a literary-source exception for རྒྱུད་.

notes.problem: མེ་དེ་ཉིད་ལ་འདུ་བར་བྱ་ directs an approach/gathering toward the same fire; it does not say to accumulate fire.
notes.treatment: Use one should approach that very fire, preserving the quotation and its paradoxical relation to being burned.
notes.uncertainty: The verb can suggest coming together with or returning to the fire; the precise analogy is not authenticated.
notes.review_action: Locate the cited tantra passage to establish the verb and simile.
